rejected.title: Standard and non-standard language
card: Standard
language that follows accepted grammar and spelling, and is common in formal writing, such as "We are going to the beach."
Non-standard
language that departs from this, such as slang ("arvo"), dialect ("we was going") or deliberately broken rules, such as a sentence fragment.
Non-standard language is not a mistake when a writer chooses it. It can build a voice, show a character's background or fit an audience.
In any form, from a story to a speech, a writer picks standard or non-standard language to suit the voice, audience and context of the piece.
rejected.remember: Non-standard language works when it is chosen on purpose to suit voice, audience and context.

a.q: A writer has a teenage narrator say "Nah, we was just hanging at the servo." What is the most likely purpose of this language?
opts: To build a casual, believable voice for the narrator
To show the writer does not know the grammar rules
To make the piece sound formal and academic
To explain a process to the reader step by step
a.why: Slang and non-standard grammar can make a narrator sound real and casual. It is not a mistake when chosen on purpose, and it does not make writing formal.
a.clue: Think about who is speaking and how they would talk.

b.q: Dan chooses to fill his speech for a school assembly, with the principal and visiting parents listening, with slang and broken grammar. What is the best criticism of this choice?
opts: It may not suit the audience and context of the assembly
It may be an error, as all non-standard language is wrong
It may give the speech a voice, which suits stories only
It may show Dan's background, which only fiction should do
b.why: Writers choose language to suit audience and context, and heavy slang may not fit an assembly with the principal and parents. It is not an error, because Dan chose it on purpose, and the card says this choice applies in any form, so voice and background are not limited to stories.
b.clue: Recall what any choice of language has to suit.

b.q: Dan writes a formal speech for a school assembly about exam stress. He fills it with slang and broken grammar. What is the main problem with this choice?
opts: It may not suit the formal context and audience
Non-standard language is always a mistake in a speech
Slang cannot be understood by anyone at school
It breaks grammar rules, which a writer may never do
b.why: Non-standard language needs to suit the audience and context, and a formal assembly may not fit it. It is not always wrong: a writer may break rules on purpose, so the other options overstate the case.
b.clue: Ask whether the language fits the occasion.
